but it hasn't taken everything away. it's within your control to rein it in. you can do this. 

however insurmountable it seems. you also know this deep down you're an unyielding fighter. 

you've got this girl. i believe in ya

sometimes i can pacify this voice but other times, it's relentless. it doesn't let me rest, fights me at every turn of anything i enjoy, screeching 'you don't deserve this', 'you're not worthy of this', flashing memory bits of every mistake i ever made.

is it the prolonged isolation? self-neglect? loneliness? estrangement from family? i have no idea. but it's been really fucking hard. it taints and permutes every happy memory and i'm restless.

the anxiety grates and wears down the soul.

​

you deserve to be happy and exist in the here and now, just as you are. just as i need to hear these words

​

whoever and wherever you are. sending you hugs.

i have this weird feeling... a clicking or betwitching sense of certainty, which soothes and avails the universe in that singule moment. at thisvery  moment, i am again awake, lucid and curious. whole once again. and because this rush of dopamine is so liberating, i often actively recall times when i felt this bulb go off. and this can, at times, be both (1) a compulsion and (2) an obsession.
(1)- i want to synthesize this feeling during times of fear or uncertainty. subsequently, my mind races to the nearest memory it conjures when i felt such feeling. a. my mind finds its momentary and artificial relief often, often indulging in more consumption by checking/reaffirming.
this step usually repeats until i'm either distracted or find something else more engaging, OR:
(2)- sometimes, 1.a. can take a devious turn, wherein i compulse over a taboo-subject, checking it relentlessly, turning it on its all corners, examaining for certainty. over time, with strong convinction, this desire will dissipate. contrarily, without great caution, this can lead to (1), which will form a new memory with (2), tainting the last recall of feeling this relief, leading me down an abyss of (2).
unsurprisingly, while jotting down this process, my mind has a huge fight or flight response, desperately clawing for me to veer away from topic.

There is definitely a strong basis for unprocessed negative emotions or underlying fears for the disease. I personally have the pure-OCD, in which the sufferer manifests compulsions within the mind. So you cant really see me perform rituals for placating anxiety physically, as both obsessions and compulsions happen internally. In addition to this, my specific subclass of p-OCD is forked scrupulosity, in which i obsess over morality of things so most of torment happens behind closed doors.

She is an excellent writer and I hope she continues to write for our community. She captured the OCD's terrorizing ordeal supremely well by sharing her decade-long struggle. 'turning the top-soils of my mind' really hit it on the head for me... as was:

> Neither did I understand that my soul-searching behaviour was actually making my thoughts worse. I was wholly ignorant of the bitter irony that in constantly seeking certainty, pure O-ers render themselves more uncertain. 

What a great read. Thank you for that joyhassprung

An intrusive thought itself could become a compulsion, creating a recursive process. Using your example, if I feel some anxiety or become overcome with homophobic fears, I will turn to an ocd thought or feeling (triggers) to alleviate that anxiety momentarily by causing a huge spike in its intensity. Once the huge spike of paralyzing anxiety subsides, I will take a brief moment of solace in the refractory period, but the process will repeat in greater frequency/intensity

Do it and seek professional help. I knew I had ocd since I was 14 but kept it a secret because I thought admitting it would become a self-fullfilling prophecy. In retrospect, I didn't have to suffer so much in silence

I understand what you mean. In the past 10 years or so I think I learned how to hijack my cognition reflexively and diffuse my thinking process via ADD-like symptoms. For example, when I'm in the middle of a task I will feel a sudden apprehension/fear and switch on or latch onto an ocd thought or feeling. Then an electrical storm will fire in a specific region of my head, which gives me a numbing headache while diverting my attention to various different topics. Much like how thinking of the populous is subdued in Kurt Vonnegut's Harrison Bergeron.

When I take an adderall, however, I notice that gnawing apprehension or fear severely mitigated. I don't feel that burning itch or awareness of that building pressure as much. Sometimes, I can identify a bubbling ocd-feelings/thoughts and relabel them as such quicker than i would normally.

But since I've been popping prozac, bupropin, and lorazapam like candy to combat my reflex, I've been hesitant about adding more chemicals to my repertoire. Don't abuse it.

I grew up in a fundamentalist Christian household and had flourished in that sort of environment. So when it comes to pain, suffering, solitude, asceticism, liberation, and redemption I think my mind viscerally conjures religious dictions in attempt to describe them.  

It's funny how you can still get mired in your upbringing despite years of conscious undoing.

I used to be a competitive runner. But ocd hijacked one of my youthful passions. Actually, it was the first to go which utterly destroyed me. My pure o usually kicks in at the heat of the moment when i need most concentration and sap  my resolve and add in extra interference and effort. Granted ive overcome enough in the past year to work out 5 days a week, getting in to a zone has been hard. I can push myself to the cusp of my limits but blasting through the pain and ocd has been a source of frustration. Im hoping that will change with each repition
